AGENDA
  GLENDALE WATER AND POWER COMMISSION
  (STAFF ACCESS ONLY) COUNCIL CHAMBERS
  613 E. Broadway, 2nd Floor
  Glendale, CA 91206
 Welcome to the meeting of the Glendale Water and Power Commission. Meetings are broadcast live
 on cable channel 6 (GTV6) and rebroadcast throughout the week. Call (818) 548-4013 for program
 schedules. DVDs of the proceedings are available for purchase in the City Clerk’s Office. Meetings
 are  also  archived  on  the  City  Website  for  viewing  anytime  at
 https://www.glendaleca.gov/government/public-meeting-portal. If you have any question about
 matters on the agenda, or requests for assistance, please contact the Glendale Water and Power
 Administration Office at (818) 548-2107 during regular business hours.
  PLEASE TURN OFF CELLULAR PHONES WHILE INSIDE THE COUNCIL CHAMBER.
 In compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) of 1990, auxiliary hearing aids, sign
 language translation, and Braille transcripts are available upon request. Assisted listening devices
 are available same-day upon request. At least 48 hours (or two business days) notice is required for
 requests regarding sign language translation and Braille transcription services. All documents related
 to open session items on this agenda that are received less than 72 hours prior to this meeting, and
 are public records, will be available for review in the Glendale Water and Power Administration Office,
 141 N. Glendale Ave., Suite 450, Glendale, CA 91206.
 Translation services are provided for meetings through the use of bilingual staff for speakers who
 wish to utilize the service as available. Speakers should state their request by contacting the City
 Clerk’s office at (818) 548-2090, at least 24 hours prior to the scheduled meeting. Please specify
 the language for which you require translation. The exclusive use of City provided interpreters is not
 required and persons are welcome to use their own interpreter or speak in their native language.
  NOVEMBER 2, 2020 AT 4:00 PM

Due to the evolving situation with the COVID-19 novel coronavirus and health recommendations from
the LA County Health Department, the Glendale Water and Power Commission meeting will be
available to the public electronically.

Due to social distancing requirements, the public will not be able to attend the meeting. The public is
encouraged to watch and participate from the safety of their homes to practice social distancing.

The meeting can be viewed:
On local cable: Charter Cable Channel 6 and AT&T U-verse Channel 99.

MINUTES
  GLENDALE WATER & POWER COMMISSION

  CITY HALL - COUNCIL CHAMBER
  613 E. Broadway, 2nd Floor, Glendale, CA 91206

  Monday, November 02, 2020, 4:00 PM

1. ROLL CALL
  The meeting was called to order at 4:04 p.m.

  Present: President Kedikian, Commissioners Flanigan and Jazmadarian

  Absent: Commissioner Avanessian and Lall

2. GWP COMMISSION/ STAFF COMMENTS
  None.

3. REPORTS – INFORMATION
  a. Legislative Update
  Mr. Leo Zalyan, Legislative Analyst, reported on key energy and water bills from the
  legislative session and listed potential bill topics for 2021. Mr. Zalyan highlighted recently
  adopted legislation, including AB 841, a transportation electrification bill that adds
  additional infrastructure to support charging stations, and SB 364, which provides a tax
  exemption to non-residential solar energy system constructed before 2025. On the water
  side, Mr. Zalyan highlighted AB 2560, which provides additional procedures for water
  quality notification and response levels.

  Commissioner Flanigan noted that he wanted to flag for GWP that AB 841 may include
  funding for schools for HVAC upgrades. In response to a question from Commissioner
  Flanigan, Mr. Zalyan explained that “procurement mandate” refers to a requirement that all
  utilities procure a certain type of energy, such as hydroelectric energy. Concerning SB
  364, President Kedikian inquired whether residential solar systems are exempt from
  taxation and Mr. Zalyan.

  b. GWP Cares Program Update
  Mr. Craig Kuennen, Deputy General Manager, presented a report regarding the GWP
  Cares Program, which provides one-time bill relief to eligible residential and commercial
  customers financially affected by COVID-19. Mr. Kuennen stated that the program was
  initially scheduled to be open from July 1 through October 30, 2020, but the program has
  been extended through December 31, 2020. Mr. Kuennen noted that GWP has received
  fewer applications than expected for the program and has only expended about 1/3 of the
  budgeted funds, described the outreach that has been done and how customers can
  apply. Mr. Kuennen also covered other supports in place to help customers struggling
  with bill payment.
  Commissioner Flanigan encouraged interested customers to apply for the GWP Cares
  1
   Program. Commissioner Jazmadarian asked if GWP might extend the program beyond
  December 2020, and Mr. Kuennen responded that GWP has the ability to do so and will
  evaluate closer to the end of the year, noting that GWP is also considering ways that the
  program might be modified to help customers, including demand charge customers.
  President Kedikian inquired about what happens to the program funding if not expended,
  and Mr. Kuennen responded that the Public Benefits Charge Program funds the program,
  and as such, funds will not be lost; the funds can be used for this program or another
  Public Benefits Charge program in a future year.

  c. Mylar Balloons Ban Update
  Ms. Dorine Martirosian, Principal Assistant City Attorney, presented a report regarding the
  mylar balloon ban recently adopted by City Council Ordinance. Ms. Martirosian covered
  existing California laws on mylar balloons, and the provisions of Glendale’s Ordinance,
  including exceptions to the ban, and GWP’s outreach and education efforts with local
  businesses.

  Commissioner Jazmadarian expressed support for the new Ordinance. President
  Kedikian inquired whether the City can add warning signs on helium tanks. Ms.
  Martirosian responded that while this is not part of the Ordinance, this is something that
  the City can discuss with store owners if they are amenable.

4. ORAL COMMUNICATIONS
  Mr. Herbert Molano (request for reporting on water pipeline management, planning and
  budgeting

5. AGENDA FORECAST
  The Commissioners reviewed the agenda forecast for the December meeting. Commissioner
  Flanigan requested a status update in December 2020 and January 2021 on the Virtual Power
  Plant program, and President Kedikian seconded the request.

6. ADJOURNMENT
  Motion to Adjourn:
  Moved by: Commissioner Jazmadarian
  Seconded by: President Kedikian
  Motion Passed.
  The meeting was adjourned at 4:37 p.m.
